aa0f5b46d2d24e21f83e9d82dcd403003e990c4b.summary: This is an index page for the Team Cymru Cybersecurity Blog research library, listing 9 of 177 articles with dates and bylines. It describes the blog's focus on threat actors, command-and-control infrastructure and ransomware, but contains no threat analysis of its own. It is not a threat report.

aa8994e9777e41653068f292c965b500a907ff18.summary: This is a project README for dirsearch, an open-source web path brute-forcer written in Python with standalone builds for Linux, Windows and macOS. It covers installation, usage, session management, Docker, building from source, CI workflows and tips for scanning. It describes a general-purpose scanning tool and does not report a threat actor, campaign, malware, vulnerability or incident, so it is not a threat report.

aaf315d67acbcdbec9f30cb18eb9d494b3c6a66f.summary: DCSO CyTec analyses a backdoored Russian-language installer, "Statistika KZU", which the authors suspect is internal Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs software for relaying consular reports. The installer carries a KONNI variant that the report links to DPRK-nexus actors, including Konni Group (TA406). The report could not verify whether the installer itself is legitimate.

aa0f49e2902cdde49e5ac0fb0e0a4602d35a0462.summary: Europol reports the arrest in Alicante, Spain, of the leader of the cybercrime gang behind the Carbanak and Cobalt malware. Since 2013 the gang attacked banks, e-payment systems and financial institutions in more than 40 countries, with cumulative losses over EUR 1 billion. The investigation was supported by Spanish National Police, the US FBI, several national authorities and private security companies.
